From Claude, not from the reviewer: the song has been redrafted with the Tibetan translation (Toh 2293) beside it, and the Tibetan of each commentary segment is now aligned too (`parallel.toh2293` on each segment in the unit JSON). The reviewer has not yet seen the previous commentary translation.

Revise the commentary translation and notes in the light of the Tibetan: translate Munidatta's Sanskrit (the reading text); where the Tibetan reads a word differently (a negative the printed Sanskrit lacks, another word, a clearer reading of a damaged or misprinted passage), record it in the segment's flags, and in the note when it changes what Munidatta says. Keep everything the Tibetan does not bear on. Make quoted song lines agree with the new draft.

Observations on the commentary from the pass that matched glossary terms to the Tibetan (check them yourself against the input):
- cp.01.m1 (siddha, grub pa): Rendered grub pa here and in grub pa'i slob dpon for siddhācārya (cp.01.m2, cp.01.m6) rather than the glossary's grub thob, and cp.01.m6 once writes ādisiddhācārya as dang po sgrub pa'i slob dpon, with sgrub.
- cp.01.m2 (kala, dus): Munidatta's sa eva kālaḥ ('he is Kāla') appears as de nyid kyi dus su, 'at that very time', so the Tibetan reads kāla as time rather than as a name for Rāhu; kālāgni in Kṛṣṇa's verse is likewise dus kyi me.
- cp.01.m2 (p-rahu, sgra gcan): The Tibetan calls Rāhu tha mal pa'i sems 'dzag pa'i rang bzhin, 'having the nature of the leaking of the ordinary mind', apparently reading cyuti, 'falling', where Shastri's text has acyutirūpo.
- cp.01.m2 (moon, ri dgas mtshan): A word-for-word calque of mṛgāṅka, 'deer-marked', rather than the ordinary zla ba.
- cp.01.m2 (p-bhagavat, bcom ldan 'das): The Tibetan construes bhagavataḥ as the agent of paripakvakuśalāḥ (bcom ldan 'das kyis dge ba rnams yongs su smin pa, 'whose virtues the Blessed One has ripened') rather than with pañcakrama, so the five stages are not called the Blessed One's.
- cp.01.m2 (patamanjari, pa Ta ha'i snye ma): Half transliterated and half translated: paṭa appears as pa Ta ha (as if paṭaha, 'drum') and mañjarī as snye ma, 'cluster', while rāga is rendered glu'i gdangs, 'melody of the song'.
- cp.01.m2 (siddhi, dngos grub): In the Rativajra verse the Tibetan has 'dod pa'i dngos grub, 'the desired accomplishment', where the Sanskrit has siddhir aninditā, 'flawless accomplishment'.
- cp.01.m2 (skandha, phung po): The Tibetan has gzugs la sogs pa'i phung po rnams, without the number five of rūpādayaḥ pañcaskandhāḥ.
- cp.01.m2 (tx-rativajra, ra ti badzra): Transliterated, and construed with the agentive (ra ti badzra gyis kyang) as if an author were speaking, where the Sanskrit has the locative rativajre, 'in the Rativajra'.
- cp.01.m2 (tx-samputa, saM puT 'byung ba'i): Half transliterated and half translated: saṃpuṭa is kept as saM puT, udbhava is rendered 'byung ba, and tantrarāja is given as rgyud kyi rgyal po.
- cp.01.m2 (yuganaddha, zung 'jug): Here zung 'jug is followed by bcings pa, 'bound' (zung 'jug bcings pa'i ngo bo), apparently rendering naddha a second time; cp.01.m6 has zung du 'jug pa'i ngo bo.
- cp.01.m3 (tx-guhyasamaja, gsang ba 'dus pa): Where the Sanskrit has the short title Śrī Samāja, the Tibetan gives the full name, dpal gsang ba 'dus pa.
- cp.01.m3 (tx-hevajra, dgyes pa'i rdo rje): Translated as dpal dgyes pa'i rdo rje (dgyes pa rdo rje in cp.01.m4), not the glossary's kye'i rdo rje'i rgyud.
- cp.01.m3 (vajra, rdo rje): Both vajra (vajraguru, rdo rje bla ma) and its synonym kuliśa (kuliśāravinda, rdo rje dang chu skyes) are rendered rdo rje in this segment.
- cp.01.m3 (viramananda, khyad par gyis dga' ba): By position the Tibetan has khyad par gyis dga' ba, 'joy through distinction', with an instrumental where the Sanskrit has the locative viramānande, and no word meaning 'cessation'.
- cp.01.m4 (tirthika, mu stegs): The verse has sangs rgyas mu stegs, but the prose after it renders buddhatīrthikaḥ as sangs rgyas pa'i mu stegs pa rnams, 'the tīrthikas of the Buddhists', reading the compound as dependent rather than as 'Buddhists and tīrthikas'.
- cp.01.m5 (maharaganaya, chags pa chen po'i tshul): Here rāga is rendered chags pa, not the 'dod chags of cp.01.m4.
- cp.01.m5 (nairatma, bdag med pa'i): The Tibetan reads bdag med pa'i chos, 'the dharma of selflessness', with bdag med pa rather than the goddess name bdag med ma, so this occurrence fits selflessness (nairatmya) better than Nairātmā.
- cp.01.m5 (pada, rkang pa): Munidatta's tṛtīyapadam, 'the third verse', appears as rkang pa gsum, 'three verses', without the ordinal pa (contrast rkang pa bzhi pas for caturthapadena in cp.01.m6).
- cp.01.m5 (sahaja, lhan skyes): A short form of the glossary's lhan cig skyes pa, in the verse Munidatta quotes.
- cp.01.m6 (moon, ri bong 'dzin pa): A calque of śaśin, 'hare-holder' (dkar po ri bong 'dzin pa), in a gloss that the Tibetan heads with zla ba, the word its song has in place of dhamaṇa.
- cp.01.m6 (tx-hevajra, brtag pa gnyis pa): Munidatta's alternative title Dvikalpa is translated brtag pa gnyis pa, kalpa rendered brtag pa, 'examination'.

Observations on the commentary from the pass that matched glossary terms to the Tibetan (check them yourself against the input):
- cp.10.m1 (nairatmya, bdag med pa'i): Munidatta's nairātmadharma is bdag med pa'i chos 'the dharma of selflessness', with the abstract bdag med pa rather than the goddess's name bdag med ma.
- cp.10.m1 (p-kanha, nag po spyod pa'i zhabs): The commentary uses the Tibetan name nag po spyod pa'i zhabs for Kṛṣṇapāda (also nag po zhabs in cp.10.m2 and nag po spyod pa pa in cp.10.m4), against the transliterated kAh+Na of verse 2b.
- cp.10.m1 (sandhya-bhasa, dgongs pa'i skad): The Tibetan renders the term as dgongs pa'i skad 'language of intention', reading sandhā/saṃdhā 'intention' rather than sandhyā 'twilight', and renders ḍombīśabda as g.yung mo'i sgra.
- cp.10.m2 (avadhuti, a wa d+hU tI): Transliterated (a wa d+hU tI) rather than translated with kun 'dar ma, here and in cp.10.m8 (a wa d+hU tI pa yongs su ma dag pa can).
- cp.10.m2 (nairatma, bdag med mar): bdag med mar renders the identification of Ḍombī with Nairātmā; later in the segment the vocative bho nairātmā is joined to the next lemma as kye bdag med ma'i grong khyer la, 'O, to Nairātmā's town'.
- cp.10.m2 (citta, sems): Munidatta's cittavaṭuka 'mind-lad' becomes a sentence, sems ni bram ze'i bu 'the mind is the brahmin boy', reusing the verse's bram ze'i bu.
- cp.10.m2 (guru-sampradaya, bla ma'i man ngag): sampradāya is rendered man ngag 'instruction', and the Tibetan reads asampradāyayogināṃ positively as man ngag thob pa'i rnal 'byor pa 'the yogin who has obtained the instruction', without the negation.
- cp.10.m2 (siddha, grub pa'i slob dpon): siddhācārya is grub pa'i slob dpon here, not the grub thob recorded in the glossary.
- cp.10.m3 (nirghrna, skyug bro ba): The Tibetan turns nirghṛṇa into one of the faults listed, skyug bro ba dang ngo tsha ba la sogs pa'i skyon dang bral ba 'free of faults such as revulsion and shame', instead of a separate predicate.
- cp.10.m3 (prajnopaya, thabs dang shes rab): The Tibetan reverses the pair to thabs dang shes rab 'means and wisdom', here and in the Hevajra quotation, unlike the glossary's shes rab dang thabs.
- cp.10.m3 (tx-hevajra, dpal dgyes pa'i rdo rje): The Tibetan names the tantra dpal dgyes pa'i rdo rje 'glorious Hevajra' (so also in cp.10.m4 and cp.10.m5), not the kye'i rdo rje'i rgyud recorded in the glossary.
- cp.10.m4 (nirmana-cakra, sprul pa'i 'khor lor): The Tibetan places the lotus in the wheel (sprul pa'i 'khor lor pad+ma 'dab ma drug cu rtsa bzhi dang ldan pa 'in the wheel of emanation, a lotus with sixty-four petals') rather than equating the two as padmaikaṃ nirmāṇacakraṃ does.
- cp.10.m5 (pada, rkang pa): The Tibetan counts as Munidatta does, rkang pa gsum pa 'third verse' for couplet 4 (and rkang pa gnyis pa for couplet 3 in cp.10.m4), leaving the refrain out.
- cp.10.m5 (svarupa, rang bzhin): The Tibetan fuses sadbhāvena svarūpāśayena into bden pa'i dngos po'i rang bzhin gyi bsam pas 'with the thought of the nature of the true thing', while the Hevajra quotation in the same segment renders svarūpa as ngo bo and ngo bo nyid.
- cp.10.m6 (svarupa, ngo bo nyid): Here nairātmadharmasvarūpa is chos thams cad bdag med pa'i ngo bo nyid, so svarūpa is ngo bo nyid, as in the Hevajra quotation of cp.10.m5, while the glosses in cp.10.m5 and cp.10.m7 use rang bzhin.
- cp.10.m6 (bhaga, b+ha ga): Transliterated (b+ha ga) and followed by pad+ma'i gnas su 'as the place of the lotus'.
- cp.10.m6 (visaya, yul): yul gyi snang ba 'appearance of objects' supports reading viṣayābhāsa for the printed ṣiṣayābhāsaṃ; in cp.10.m2 the Tibetan has no word for viṣaya.
- cp.10.m6 (samsara, 'khor ba'i): saṃsārapeṭaka 'the basket (or box) of saṃsāra' is rendered 'khor ba'i mdzod 'the treasury of saṃsāra'.
- cp.10.m7 (carya, spyod pa): saprapañcacaryā is rendered spyod pa rab tu gsal bar gsungs 'explains the conduct very clearly', so saprapañca is read as describing the explanation rather than the conduct.
- cp.10.m7 (kapalika, thod pa can): Here kāpālikaḥ caryādharaś ca becomes thod pa can gyi spyod pa 'dzin pa 'holding the conduct of a skull-bearer', and the Tibetan keeps Munidatta's letter-etymology in transliteration (kaM 'your bliss', pA 'able to protect').
- cp.10.m7 (tathagata, de bzhin gshegs pa): The Tibetan reads the compound as 'the wheel of the six tathāgatas' (de bzhin gshegs pa drug gi 'khor lo), followed by earrings, necklace and bone ornaments (rus rgyan).
- cp.10.m8 (guru-sampradaya, bla ma'i drin): For gurusampradāyavihīnasya the Tibetan has bla ma'i drin gyis rnam par dman pa, with drin 'kindness, grace' where cp.10.m2 has man ngag, and its syntax ('deficient by the guru's grace') is loose.

Observations on the commentary from the pass that matched glossary terms to the Tibetan (check them yourself against the input):
- cp.14.m1 (siddha, grub pa'i): siddhācārya is rendered grub pa'i slob dpon, with grub pa rather than grub thob, the Tibetan form already in the glossary.
- cp.14.m2 (boat, gru): Later in the same segment 'khor ba'i gru la, 'on the boat of saṃsāra', stands where the Sanskrit has saṃsārārṇave, 'in the ocean of saṃsāra', so the Tibetan has a boat in place of the ocean.
- cp.14.m2 (abhasa, snang ba): candrābhāsasūryābhāsau is rendered zla ba dang nyi ma'i snang ba with a single snang ba, and m5's three appearances are snang ba gsum.
- cp.14.m2 (avadhuti, a wa d+hU tI'i): Here the Tibetan transliterates avadhūtī (a wa d+hU tI) instead of using kun 'dar ma, the form in the glossary; the term was not listed for this segment because the folio number [22ka] splits the Bengali word.
- cp.14.m2 (viramananda, khyad par gyi dga' ba): viramānanda is rendered khyad par gyi dga' ba, 'distinctive joy', here and in m3, a name that says nothing of cessation and is worth checking against the glossary's 'joy of cessation'.
- cp.14.m2 (sahaja, lhan cig skyes pa'i): For sahajayānapramattāṅgī the Tibetan has lhan cig skyes pa'i chang gi btung ba, 'the liquor drink of the innate', as if reading -pāna- 'drink' for -yāna- 'vehicle'.
- cp.14.m2 (sandhya-bhasa, dgongs pa'i skad): dgongs pa'i skad, 'language of intention', reflects the sense sandhā 'intention' rather than sandhyā 'twilight', and m1 uses the same phrase for vyāja, 'guise'.
- cp.14.m2 (dombi, g.yung mo): Where the song lines transliterate Dom+bi, the commentary renders ḍomvī nairātmā as gdol pa'i bu mo g.yung mo bdag med ma, so ḍombī is translated by g.yung mo, 'low-caste woman', perhaps together with gdol pa'i bu mo, 'outcaste girl'.
- cp.14.m3 (dhruvapada, brtan pa'i rkang pas): A literal calque, with brtan pa, 'firm', for dhruva and rkang pa, 'foot, verse', for pada.
- cp.14.m4 (sahajananda, lhan cig skyes pa'i dga' bas): The Tibetan says bodhicitta is rnam par bzung, 'held', by innate joy, where the Sanskrit has vivṛtaṃ, 'opened', perhaps reading vidhṛtaṃ.
- cp.14.m4 (manimula, nor bu'i rtsa bar): The Tibetan gdang bu ni nor bu'i rtsa bar gyur pa makes the kacchikā (gdang bu, the verse's kācchī) the thing that has reached or become the root of the jewel, a looser construal of kacchikāmaṇimūlaṃ gataṃ.
- cp.14.m4 (abhiseka, dbang bskur ba): caturthābhiṣekeṇa is rendered dbang bzhi pas dbang bskur ba, 'empowered by the fourth empowerment', using both dbang and dbang bskur ba; the term was not listed for this segment because of the vowel sandhi in caturth-ābhiṣekeṇa.
- cp.14.m4 (visaya, yul): The Tibetan says the water, a stirring toward objects (yul la g.yo ba), does not enter (mi 'jug) the yogi's body, a negative that the printed Sanskrit (viśati, 'enters') lacks but that matches the verse's na paisai.
- cp.14.m5 (vilaksana, mtshan nyid dang bral bas): vilakṣaṇa is rendered by its etymology, mtshan nyid dang bral ba, 'free of characteristics'.
- cp.14.m5 (pada, rkang pa): rkang pa renders pada throughout: couplets 3, 4 and 5 are the second, third and fourth rkang pa (m4, m5, m6), and the refrain is brtan pa'i rkang pa (m3).
- cp.14.m6 (kula-shore, ngogs): kule śarīre is rendered lus kyi ngogs su, 'on the bank of the body', and the Tibetan ends with the ignorant sinking at the bank (ngogs su 'bying), echoing the verse.
- cp.14.m6 (nairatmya, bdag med pa'i): The Tibetan distinguishes the two occurrences of nairātmadharma in this segment: the first is bdag med pa'i chos, 'the dharma of selflessness', the second bdag med ma'i chos, 'the dharma of Nairātmā'.
